_comment: Curated candidate list for the New World wave (Peru / Maya / Aztec first).
PRODUCED BY: an IA advancedsearch enumeration over ~54 named works from the
corpus survey, then a hand subject-filter — import-workflow.md step 3, because
keyword enumeration is noisy (a 'Torquemada monarquia indiana' query returns
eight volumes of Quiros's Pacific voyages).
SELECTION RULES APPLIED:
- Earliest available edition wins (ad fontes). Where only a 19th-century
scholarly edition exists, that is taken and marked as such.
- Nothing printed after 1928 — a public-domain LABEL on IA is an uploader
claim, not a rights determination. This excluded the 2008 Getty Murua
facsimile and the 1930 Ximenez, both of which IA marks PD.
- Nothing with imagecount 0 (metadata-only or text-only uploads).
- Nothing already held: checked per candidate against source_fingerprint
'ia:<id>' and ia_identifier at enumeration time.
LANGUAGE FIELDS follow .claude/docs/invariants/language-fields.md:
language = the EDITION's language; original_language = the source work's;
text_role says which of the two this scan is. Markham's English Cieza is a
translation edition of a Spanish work and must not be filed as Spanish.
KNOWN STILL-MISSING after this wave (no open scan found via IA):
Torquemada Monarquia Indiana; Betanzos; Sarmiento de Gamboa; Cristobal de
Molina; Chimalpahin; Olmos; Domingo de Santo Tomas; Mendieta; Sepulveda's
Democrates alter; Munoz Camargo's Codice Ramirez. Next door for these is
Biblioteca Digital Hispanica and Google Books, not IA.

books.title: La Araucana, partes primera a quinta
